The defendant-petitioner contested the suit contending, inter alia, that plaintiff-respondent No.1 is not the legally married wife of the defendant-petitioner and plaintiff-respondent No.2, Manik Kumar Boyragi, is not the son of the defendant-petitioner. The defendant-petitioner denied the paternity of the child filing a written statement stating that on false allegations, the plaintiff-respondents instituted the present suit. The Family Court after trial decreed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 29.10.2013. 

 4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree, the defendant preferred Family Appeal No.12 of 2013 in the Court of District Judge, Pirojpur. The learned District Judge during pendency of the appeal passed an order on 06.08.2015 directing to conduct DNA test of plaintiff-respondent No.2 with the defendant-petitioner and plaintiff-respondent No.1 to ascertain the paternity. Accordingly, on 18.04.2016, the National Forensic DNA Laboratory, Dhaka submitted its report stating that the defendant-petitioner is the biological father of plaintiff-respondent No.2. Thereafter, the defendant-petitioner on 11.08.2016 submitted a written objection against the report of the DNA test and the learned Appellate Court hearing the same rejected the application on 13.10.2016. Thereafter, on 10.11.2016 the defendant-petitioner filed an application for DNA test afresh to determine paternity of the child stating that the earlier DNA report does not specify the specimen and sample obtained for the DNA test and the DNA report itself was not endorsed by the higher officer. The learned District Judge, Pirojpur hearing that application rejected the same by the impugned judgment and order dated 10.11.2016. 

 8. It appears the plaintiff-respondent, Pallabi Rani Boyragi, has come with an allegation that she was given in marriage with the defendant-petitioner, Manas Kumar Boyragi, on 24.10.2004 and the marriage was duly consummated. It has been further alleged that during the subsistence of such marriage, plaintiff-respondent No.1 gave birth a child on 27.10.2005. It has been further alleged that due to ill advice of the parents, the defendant- petitioner drove the plaintiff-respondents out the residence and as such, this suit was filed for maintenance and other allied reliefs. On the other hand, the defendant-petitioner denied the aforesaid fact of marriage consummated between them and also denied the fact of paternity. In spite of that, the Family Court decreed the suit on contest.
